chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Abu Ja'far, from his father, from Abd Allah ibn al-Fadl al-Nawfali, from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah and others, from some of his teachers, who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'Do I separate [the prayers] in the Witr?' He said: 'Yes.' I said: 'For sometimes I become thirsty and drink water.' He said: 'Yes, and marry [a woman].'

key_terms.أَفْصِلُ: I separate/divide (referring to performing rak'ahs separately)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on performing separate rak'ahs for Witr prayer and drinking water during the night?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the flexibility of the Witr prayer, permitting it to be performed as separate rak'ahs rather than a single unit. He further illustrates the leniency in night prayers by allowing the consumption of water even if it breaks a voluntary fast or ritual state, concluding with 'and marry' to highlight that marital acts are permissible and do not invalidate the spiritual merit of night worship. This reflects the Shia juristic view that Witr is a recommended (mustahabb) act with flexible execution, emphasizing ease over rigid constraint.
